baseline.commit: b2016ad (the tested tree; the final release commit differs from it only by these two evidence documents themselves - see the circularity note in docs/store-evidence.md section 5)
baseline.note: The manifest state, the acceptance procedure, the acceptance results and the boundary cases below all describe this version only; no other version is referenced.

isolation.mechanism: DSH_HOME pointed at a throwaway directory for every command, so install, start and uninstall never touch the daily profiles/

manifest.peerDependenciesMeta: every entry is optional, so an installer that resolves peers automatically writes no copy of a host package into the profile

rangeShape.oneString: engines.dsh and dsh.compatibility.dsh deliberately read the same string. From DSH 0.2.0 on, install and startup judge compatibility by engines.dsh when it is declared, so the peers are declarative and the two declared strings must not disagree with the gate.
rangeShape.upperBound: none: the range is an OR chain of one lower bound per published release line (>=0.2.0-rc.1 || >=0.2.1-rc.1 || >=0.2.2-rc.1), which accepts 0.2.0-rc.1 and everything after it. The earlier <0.3.0-0 form existed only to exclude 0.3.0's prereleases under semver.satisfies(..., { includePrerelease: true }); with no upper bound that question no longer arises, and the trade is accepted: the manifest no longer equals the tested set, which is what dshReleases records.
rangeShape.lowerBound: >=0.2.0-rc.1: the chain starts at the first release candidate of the 0.2.0 line. 1.4.2 restores the three-line OR chain, so 0.2.0-rc.1 and 0.2.0-rc.2 are inside the declared range again - they are not in the tested window, and being installable is not the same as being verified.

manifest.platformShape: dsh.client.platform stays "web" because the desktop client runs the same web client and the same client/client.js build; the two clients are declared as profiles, not as platforms

clients.shared: both run the same client artifact (client/client.js) and the same host interface; they differ only in how the plugin is installed and removed
clients.web: command line: dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-worktree-space, dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-worktree-space
clients.desktop: the plugin management page: sidebar -> Plugins -> put dsh-worktree-space in Plugin package name -> Install; to remove it, open Worktree Space from the list, go to its Plugin details page, and press Uninstall at the top right

lifecycleMatrix.note: the store contract's clause 8 requires install -> configuration -> visible -> uninstall/rollback in a disposable profile, and unit tests do not substitute for it. Each row below comes from an actual run on that release's own DSH CLI, per docs/store-evidence.md sections 1 and 2.

web.artifactNote: the tested artifact is the one this release ships: check:tracked-bundle rebuilt and compared byte-for-byte with the committed client/client.js (17E66E3C...7E08, 392359 bytes) and lib/index.js (AF9D1AE6...8ED8, 442648 bytes), and unpacking the tested tarball gives those same two hashes
web.reportNote: this run passed -Json, so the matrix-report.json beside the markdown is from the same run (pluginVersion 1.4.2, commit b2016ad, 5 versions)
web.windowNote: the window is the newest five published DSH releases, compared with the manifest's dshReleases before every run; a drift fails the run instead of silently carrying the previous window

lifecycleMatrix.desktop: confirmed by the author outside this run; the desktop lifecycle does not go through the command line

probePreconditions.sessionCookie: the launch token is exchanged for a dsh-auth-* cookie on the first index request; without replaying that cookie every /api route answers 405 on POST and 404 on GET, including host routes that are certainly registered, so that response is the auth fence and not a missing route
probePreconditions.envelopeMethod: endpointFromPath('/api', p) is p.slice('/api'.length + 1), so the envelope's method is the whole remainder, 'dsh-worktree-space/<endpoint>'; sending only '<endpoint>' is rejected with 'RPC method does not match endpoint.'
probePreconditions.bundleUrl: the client bundle address is page-relative: plugins/??dsh-worktree-space/client.js&rev=<rev>, with a per-version rev

requiredCases.unauthenticated-401: not applicable: the plugin registers no webServer and no HTTP lifecycle surface of its own; its routes ride the host's authenticated /api carrier
requiredCases.crash-recovery: not applicable: the plugin keeps no durable operation journal; each route call is one git pass, and a stopped finish is re-read from the repository's own state
requiredCases.windows-file-lock: did not trigger: in all four runs the start, the probes and the stop left no holder behind, and node_modules was removable
requiredCases.rollback-failure: did not trigger: in all four runs node_modules disappeared, cordis.patch.yml went back to 0 mentions, and --dump-config returned to its pre-install line count
requiredCases.pnpm-10: not tested: only the host-bundled pnpm was present
requiredCases.pnpm-11: not tested: only the host-bundled pnpm was present
requiredCases.pnpm-12: tested: 12.6.0, the version the host bundles; all four installs used it
requiredCases.monorepo-subpath: not applicable: this plugin installs as a single package, not from a monorepo subpath

notCovered: the end-to-end functional acceptance in docs/store-evidence.md section 2.3 has not been run this round: creating a task space, finishing a task, the two container-root checks and the task-space-location write-back all move Git repositories and are a layer above this matrix

UI-level visibility was not checked item by item: this round established the three machine-readable criteria (page reachable, bundle actually served, host RPC route registered), while the name, description and icon.svg in the plugin list, the nine configuration fields taking effect immediately, and the sidebar entry still need the walkthrough in section 2.3
only pnpm 12.6.0 was exercised; 10 and 11 were not installed and not tested
--dump-config line counts are host-version dependent and do not carry across DSH versions or across changes to the config fields

the window is the currently published releases, not a fixed set: as of 1.3.2 it covers 0.2.0-rc.1, 0.2.0-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.1 and 0.2.1-rc.2 - four, because support for the 0.1.7 line was dropped rather than because upstream published something new - and it does not follow a new upstream release automatically
the desktop lifecycle was confirmed by the author outside this run; this matrix carries command-line evidence for the web client only
